one_liner: Open-source Python library for building, evaluating, profiling, and optimizing multi-agent AI workflows across any framework.
what: NVIDIA's open-source Python toolkit (pip install nvidia-nat) for orchestrating multi-agent AI workflows. Framework-agnostic — wraps LangChain, LlamaIndex, CrewAI, Semantic Kernel, Google ADK. Provides deep MCP integration (client + server), A2A (Agent-to-Agent) protocol support, profiling/observability, evaluation tools, RL-based optimization, and a hybrid architecture using frontier models for orchestration + Nemotron open models for research tasks. Announced at GTC 2026 with Adobe, SAP, Salesforce, ServiceNow among 17 enterprise adopters.
reasoning: AIQ solves enterprise Python agent workflow orchestration — connecting, profiling, and optimizing teams of Python-based AI agents. Our L-Thread Orchestrator is fundamentally different: we run Claude Code CLI processes in tmux windows with shell scripts and git worktrees. We don't use Python agent frameworks (LangChain, CrewAI, etc.) and our 'agents' are autonomous Claude Code instances, not Python function chains. The MCP/A2A protocol support is the most interesting aspect but Claude Code already has native MCP support. The profiling and optimization features target latency/token efficiency in LLM API call chains, not coding agent task orchestration. GPU-optimized features (Dynamo integration, Agent Performance Primitives) require NVIDIA hardware we don't use. Worth watching because: (1) MCP/A2A standards convergence matters, (2) if we ever move to a Python-based orchestration layer, AIQ's evaluation and profiling tools could be valuable, (3) NVIDIA backing means this ecosystem will grow.
